items.title: Louis Tio Interview, 1960-10-26
items.q: Barney Begard was a scholar, my brother. Yes, Barney talks about it.

ctx.x: Eddie Sherry, he played with the police band. And he was also a scholar, my brother. Barney Begard was a scholar, my brother. Yes, Barney talks about it.

items.title: Louis Tio Interview, 1960-10-26
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Oh, yes. I know Barney Bigard told me that he sold a lot of numbers to Ellington...

ctx.x: So he didn't need all of them, you see. So, uh, that made him kind of a thing, because Dully wanted him to be a bandwriters in the Eagle, Illinois, but then he, he didn't care about that because he wasn't married and his wife was about to have a child. And he even figured I was going in the army, so he decided he'd come back here again. And also he'd written a lot of numbers.

Oh, yes. I know Barney Bigard told me that he sold a lot of numbers to Ellington, or quite a few, anyway. Do you remember which numbers those were? Did he ever tell you which ones he sold? Later, Duke put his name on them, and then Barney put his name on, I think, Mood Indigo or something.

Mood Indigo was right. Well, that's what he made, he sold, a sophisticated lady was originally written by Lorenzo Keough, and that was written right here on Havana Street at 2404. That was before he went to New York. Then he had Mood Indigo and Mood Glow, and him and Steve Lewis, which I would like that they made a number of, uh, Lorenzo Teo and Steve Lewis, Harlem Hot Shot. You tell me it was a pretty hot number. That was the title of it? That was the title of it. Harlem Hot Shot. I never heard, I never know…
